calls.name: ice-state-01
calls.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: the constructed "Advancing ice" state of an existing portrait game landscape.
Image 1 is the exact scene to edit. Image 2 is ONLY a reference for the small branching inheritance motif; do not import cells, a cream panel, or an icon into the landscape.
Preserve image 1's composition, camera, portrait proportions, gouache/ink style, hooked ochre headland at left, arched sea cave, paired-crater Moon, distant mountain summits, sea and the entire calm lower working area. Make one localized landscape change.
Extend the existing upper-right mountain glacier down through the right-hand forest as one connected broad icy tongue, with pale blue-white crevassed ice. It descends from the visible mountain snowfield toward the wooded shore, ending ABOVE the water at roughly 35 percent of full image height. Its front is a substantial scalloped glacial edge. It physically covers some trees in its path but retains green woodland on either side. Do not turn the entire scene into a generic snow scene or change its season globally. The new tongue should lie mainly between 44 and 93 percent of the width, from 13 to 35 percent of the height.
At the habitable ochre ground immediately beside the glacier's lower edge, show three related small brown mammals like the existing mammals, all alive together. One has a visibly thicker shaggy coat, another a smoother thinner coat, and the third is intermediate. Preserve mammal anatomy and natural scale within this landscape. These are existing inherited differences, not an animal transforming.
Add a small deliberate lapis-blue forked lineage stroke, with tiny arrowheads, between these related mammals as a restrained naturalist's atlas annotation. Echo the shape of image 2's fork. Give one endpoint a subtle coral/ochre difference-mark. No labels, no words, no numbers, no circles, no medallion, no cream rectangle, no glowing magic or dotted UI outline. The fork should be readable but subordinate to the real animals and glacier.
Keep the full landscape intact, with the warm rock and blue-green sea colours of image 1. No other animals or human structures. Retain the original wide quiet lower half.
